strong.name: Strong
strong.definition: Meta-analyses of classroom studies show that teaching this way improves learning.

promising.name: Promising
promising.definition: Controlled studies show gains, but results are mixed, small in number or dependent on context.

framework.name: Framework
framework.definition: A useful structure for planning, with no intervention studies behind it as a method.

theory.name: Theory
theory.definition: A way of explaining how learning happens. It shapes values and choices, but cannot be tested as a single intervention.

school.name: School model
school.definition: A whole-school movement with its own philosophy and practice.

contested.name: Contested
contested.definition: The research does not support using it as a teaching method, even though many teachers believe in it.

problems.name: They forget everything by the test
problems.what_it_looks_like: Students seemed to understand in the lesson, but two weeks later it has gone, and the test shows it.

problems.name: They don't get started
problems.what_it_looks_like: The task is set, and half the class sits looking at it, asks what to do or waits for help.

problems.name: Discussions die
problems.what_it_looks_like: You ask a good question, the same three students answer, and the rest wait for it to be over.

problems.name: Mixed levels in one class
problems.what_it_looks_like: Some students are finished in five minutes, others have not understood the first step.

problems.name: They copy AI answers
problems.what_it_looks_like: Homework is fluent and correct, but students cannot explain it, and tests do not match it.

problems.name: My lessons overload them
problems.what_it_looks_like: Slides full of text, many new terms at once, and blank faces halfway through.

problems.name: They can do it with me, but not alone
problems.what_it_looks_like: With you at their side it goes well. On their own, or in a new task, it falls apart.

problems.name: They don't know what good work looks like
problems.what_it_looks_like: Students hand in work that misses the point and are surprised by the grade.

problems.name: Some students have stopped trying
problems.what_it_looks_like: A few students have decided the subject is not for them and no longer try.

problems.name: I can't tell who has understood until the test
problems.what_it_looks_like: The lesson felt fine, nods all round, and then the test shows that many did not get it.

recipes.name: The knowledge lesson
steps: Open with three retrieval questions from earlier lessons (5 min).
Explain and model the new idea in small steps, with one worked example (15 min).
Guided practice with a half-finished example, checking as you go (10 min).
Independent practice, then one exit question on today's goal (15 min).

recipes.name: The discussion lesson
steps: One open question that has more than one good answer.
Think alone first (2 min), then talk in pairs (5 min).
Whole-class discussion where students build on each other's answers (15 min).
A hinge question at the end shows whether the key idea has landed (5 min).

recipes.name: The practice lesson
steps: A short quiz from memory, mixing this week and earlier weeks (8 min).
Students check their own answers against a key and mark what they missed (5 min).
Mixed practice where students must choose the method, not just apply it (20 min).
Feedback on one thing to do differently next time (10 min).
